diagnostic_evidence.quote: Given an $m$-Hausdorff rectifiable set $S\subset \R^{d}$, the unique current associated with it is defined as $[S]\in  \Omega_{0}^{m}(\R^{d})^{*} $
\tau^{S}(x) := e_{1}(x)\edge \dots e_{m}(x), a wedge product of orthonomal basis vectors of the tangent space at $x$.

issues.failure_explanation: An orientation-reversing change of an orthonormal tangent basis multiplies e_1\wedge\dots\wedge e_m by -1. A general m-rectifiable set has no canonical orientation, so [S] is not well-defined as stated.

failure_location.quote: the choice of basis vectors does not matter due to invariance of wedge product under change of orthonomal basis.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Require S to be oriented, or fix a measurable orientation/outward normal for the triangulated surfaces before defining [S].
issues.overall_effect: The background current representation is not well-defined for unoriented rectifiable sets; later uses only work after an unstated orientation choice.
issues.title: Unoriented rectifiable sets assigned a canonical current
issues.why_classification: Adding a standard orientation hypothesis is local and preserves the subsequent oriented surface and normal-cycle arguments.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Indeed, the distance \cref{currdualmet} simply collapses to the sum of Hausdorff measure of each shape.

issues.failure_explanation: A dual norm is a supremum over the unit ball. As written, the supremum over all differential forms is infinite for distinct currents. Even after adding the unit-ball constraint, the distance for S=T is 0, not the sum of the two Hausdorff measures.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the supremum to forms with \lVert\omega\rVert_\infty\le 1 and replace the claim with the correct mass bound or mass-of-difference interpretation.
issues.overall_effect: The uniform-norm current distance is not the finite quantity claimed, and its stated interpretation as a sum of Hausdorff measures is false.
issues.title: Current dual norm defined without unit-ball restriction and misidentified
issues.why_classification: The repair is a local correction of a background definition and does not alter the main normal-cycle compression method or rates.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: where $(e_{1}(x,u),e_{2}(x,u),u)$ is a positively oriented orthonomal basis of $\R^{3}$.

issues.failure_explanation: For t=f/|f| and u perpendicular to t, det(t, t\times u, u)=-1. The displayed frame is left-handed, so the derived cylindrical 2-vector \tau and the integrated weight \gamma have the wrong sign.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use e_2=u\times(f/|f|), or equivalently reverse the sign of the cylindrical contribution in the final decomposition.
issues.overall_effect: The cylindrical Dirac weights used in the claimed normal-cycle decomposition are unreliable, and the embedded functional F(N(T)) inherits the sign error.
issues.title: Cylindrical frame declared positive but has negative orientation
issues.why_classification: This is a local orientation/sign correction in the construction; it does not require new proof architecture if the intended decomposition is retained.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: As $(e_{1}(x,u),e_{2}(x,u),u)$ is a positively oriented orthonomal basis, it implies $u = e_{1}(x,u) \times e_{2}(x,u)$.

issues.failure_explanation: For a positively oriented frame, p\wedge q = u_1 e_2\wedge e_3 - u_2 e_1\wedge e_3 + u_3 e_1\wedge e_2. The displayed +u_2 e_1\wedge e_3 term has the wrong sign; for example u=e_2 gives the opposite 2-vector.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Change the u_2 term to -u_2\begin{pmatrix}0\\e_1\end{pmatrix}\wedge\begin{pmatrix}0\\e_3\end{pmatrix}, or adjust the definition of \tilde b_2 consistently.
issues.overall_effect: The boundary/spherical weights \alpha_k, and hence the Dirac delta form and the embedded normal cycle, are incorrect.
issues.title: Spherical coordinate expansion has wrong sign in the u_2 term
issues.why_classification: This is a local sign correction in the coordinate computation; the rest of the construction can survive if the sign is fixed.

issues.failure_explanation: The cylindrical component is stated as -\pi/2 \sum \delta_{c_j}\gamma_j using the pre-redefinition \gamma_j. The final \gamma_i is then defined as the negative of that quantity, so the cylindrical contribution in the final variables should be +\pi/2 \sum \delta_{c_i}\gamma_i, not +\pi \sum \delta_{c_i}\gamma_i.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the edge coefficient \pi in \cref{NC_delta} by \pi/2 and propagate the same correction to \cref{realembedding}.
issues.overall_effect: The interior edge part of the claimed normal-cycle delta decomposition is scaled incorrectly, so the functional passed to compression is not the stated N(T).
issues.title: Cylindrical coefficient in the Dirac delta form is off by a factor of 2
issues.why_classification: The repair is a local coefficient correction; it does not change the algorithmic method or the general compression guarantee once the correct weights are used.

issues.failure_explanation: The spherical component is derived as -\pi \sum \delta_{x_k}\alpha_k using the pre-redefinition \alpha_k. The final \alpha_i is defined as the negative of that quantity, so the boundary contribution should be +\pi \sum \delta_{x_i}\alpha_i. The embedding uses \pi/2 instead.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Change the boundary coefficient in \cref{realembedding} from \pi/2 to \pi, or correct the preceding spherical-component coefficient consistently.
issues.overall_effect: The embedded functional F(N(T)) has incorrect boundary weights, so the compression approximates a different functional on the boundary part.
issues.title: Boundary coefficient in the real-valued embedding is off by a factor of 2
issues.why_classification: This is a local coefficient mismatch in the final embedding; the compression construction itself does not need to be redesigned.

issues.failure_explanation: The symbol \hat{\alpha}_i is never defined. Under the natural repair \hat{\alpha}_i=\alpha_i, the left-hand side is \alpha^{T}(K_{XX}-Q_{XX})\alpha, which cannot be bounded by a constant times tr(K_{XX}-Q_{XX}) uniformly over arbitrary \alpha. For example, take k(x_i,x_j)=\delta_{ij}, C={x_1}, and \alpha=M e_2; the error is M^2 while tr(K_{XX}-Q_{XX})=n-1. The theorem therefore lacks a necessary weight-dependent hypothesis or factor.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must define \hat{\alpha} and either add a proved uniform bound on the weights or replace the bound with a valid instance-dependent estimate involving \lVert\alpha\rVert.
issues.overall_effect: The main theoretical guarantee for RLS compression, and the advertised error decay for arbitrary discrete normal-cycle weights, are unsupported; the algorithm's stated guarantee is unreliable as written.
issues.title: Compression theorem uses undefined weights and an unsupported alpha-independent bound
issues.why_classification: The failure changes the central guarantee from an alpha-independent trace/eigenvalue bound to an instance-dependent one, and the source does not provide the missing hypothesis or proof.

issues.failure_explanation: The reported full and compressed Hausdorff scores are 0.0442 and 0.0298, a 33% reduction. They are not near identical, so the prose overstates the equivalence of the matching quality.

failure_location.quote: This is numerically evidenced by the near identical Hausdorff metric score.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Revise the sentence to say the Hausdorff scores are comparable or that the compressed match improves the score.
issues.overall_effect: The claim that compressed matching quality is nearly identical to full matching is supported only as comparable or better, not as near identical.
issues.title: Prose calls materially different Hausdorff scores near identical
issues.why_classification: This is a local prose correction; the numerical results themselves remain usable if the wording is made consistent with the reported values.
